probes.description: StockTransfer lifecycle declares only Draft->Committed: that transition succeeds, but Committed->Draft is refused with 422 CONCEPT_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_INVALID and the stored row keeps status Committed (a schema-accepted lifecycle that is not enforced would let the write through).

A create that omits the status field gets the state flagged initial:true (Draft) instead of being refused as a missing required field, and a state value that is not a declared lifecycle state is rejected with 422.

PATCH /api/concepts/StockTransfer/batch runs the same lifecycle gate as the single-record PUT: an allowed Draft->Committed op is reported updated and persisted, an illegal Committed->Draft op is reported failed (reason names the transition) and the row stays Committed.

WidgetOrderLine.PositiveQuantity (quantity > 0) is enforced on create: quantity 0 is refused with 422 invariant_failed naming PositiveQuantity at path quantity, and quantity 2 is accepted (so the refusal is the invariant, not a blanket failure).
An UPDATE that would violate PositiveQuantity is refused (422 invariant_failed) and the stored row keeps its previous quantity and version - the invariant is not create-only.

PATCH /api/concepts/WidgetOrderLine/batch applies the same invariants as the single-record PUT: quantity 0 is reported failed (reason names the rejected invariant) and the row is unchanged, while a valid batch op (quantity 7) is reported updated and persisted.

ActiveCatalogEntries (where discontinued == false) returns the active row and never a discontinued one: the discontinued fixture sorts FIRST by sku, so an ignored/unapplied where would surface it at rows[0] and as a '"discontinued":true' fragment.

ActiveCatalogEntries orderBy sku (ascending): three rows created out of order come back sorted, and the limit/offset request parameters window the sorted set (limit=1&offset=1 is the middle row, offset=2 the last, limit=2 returns exactly two rows).

ShippedUnitsByWarehouseMonth: the group QIL-AGG/2026-03 reports exact sum 3e9, avg 1.5e9, min 1e9, max 2e9, count 2 - the 0 and -7 events the query where (unitsShipped > 0) must drop would change count, min and sum if the where were ignored.

groupBy [warehouseId, {shippedAt, bucket: month}] yields one row per (warehouse, month): same-month events collapse (QIL-AGG March), another month stays separate (QIL-AGG April = 1e8), and another warehouse in the same month is its own row; the bucketed key is rendered as yyyy-MM and the echo lists the bucket.
ShippedUnitsByWarehouseMonth orderBy 'totalUnits desc': groups of 3e9, 5e8 and 1e8 units, inserted ascending, come back strictly descending (an ignored orderBy would return insertion/group order).

WarehouseMonthShareOfAllTime on warehouse QIL-SHR (Mar +40/-10, Apr +60, May -25): the lookup allTimeUnits sums only unitsShipped > 0 per warehouse (= 100, would be 65 if its where were ignored) and the computed column sharePercent = monthUnits*100/allTimeUnits is exactly 30 for March and 60 for April.

having 'sharePercent > 0' (a computed column) drops the QIL-SHR May group (monthUnits -25 => share -25) while the March and April groups of the same warehouse remain - the having is applied after lookups/computed, per the schema.

POST .../check-balances/OrigemDestinoBalance on a two-sku draft reports each [sku, validity] group separately with exact left/right totals and delta (A1: Origem 5 vs Destino 3 => delta 2, unbalanced, templated message 'Faltam 2 unidade(s) de A1 (validade 2027-01-01) no destino'; B2: 4 vs 4 => balanced) and does not persist anything.

json.$.__balances.OrigemDestinoBalance.groups: Faltam 2 unidade(s) de A1 (validade 2027-01-01) no destino

probes.description: Committing a StockTransferAggregate draft whose position quantity (50) exceeds the available stock (10, from the AvailableQuantityQuery lookup field) is vetoed by the aggregate invariant PositionWithinAvailable (message names the rule) and nothing is persisted - not even the root. (Status code of the veto is tracked separately: qil-aggregate-veto-status-is-client-error.)

Committing an unbalanced draft (Origem 5, Destino 3, both within available stock) is vetoed server-side by the balance rule with its templated shortfall message, and nothing is persisted - the server never trusts the client's check-balances.

$.message.matches: balance\(s\) violated: Faltam 2 unidade\(s\) de A1 \(validade 2027-01-01\) no destino

probes.description: A balanced, within-stock draft commits (200): the root and both positions are persisted with generated ids and the childField links (items.stockTransferId, positions.stockTransferItemId), and each position carries the query-sourced lookup field maxQuantity = 10 (from StockLocation.disponivel via AvailableQuantityQuery joined on localId). The root is then readable through the plain concept endpoint.

The aggregate commit path honours the root concept's lifecycle: re-committing a Committed StockTransfer with status Draft (balanced, within stock) does not change the stored status - the row stays Committed and no child rows are written. (The HTTP status of that refusal is tracked in qil-aggregate-lifecycle-refusal-is-client-error.)

DEFECT: an aggregate invariant/balance veto is a client error, but POST /api/runtime/aggregate/StockTransferAggregate answers 503 Service Unavailable (AggregateApiController maps every IllegalStateException to 503, including the veto thrown by assertAggregateInvariants/assertAggregateBalances). Request: draft with quantity 50 > disponivel 10. Actual: 503 {"message":"Aggregate StockTransferAggregate invariant(s) violated: PositionWithinAvailable -- ..."}. Expected: 4xx (400/409/422).

DEFECT: committing an aggregate draft that moves the root Committed->Draft is refused (row unchanged) but answers a bare 500 Internal Server Error {"status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","path":"/api/runtime/aggregate/StockTransferAggregate"} - the single-record endpoints answer 422 CONCEPT_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_INVALID. Expected a 4xx.

DEFECT: AggregateRuntime.commit documents that a failing onCommit procedure rolls back every prior write of the commit (root and children). Request: POST /api/runtime/aggregate/WidgetOrderAggregate with an explicit root id and one line while no WidgetOrderAudit row exists, so AuditWidgetOrderProcedure fails (503 'onCommit procedure ... failed: CONCEPT_NOT_FOUND'). Actual: after the 503 the WidgetOrder (GET /api/widget_orders/<id> 200) and its WidgetOrderLine are still stored. Expected: both 404. (Uses throwaway StockTransfer ids as uuid sources.)

WidgetOrder.orderNumber defaults to nextNumber('orderNumber') (format ORD-{year}-{seq:4}, tenant scope): two orders created one after the other each get a number of the declared shape, the numbers differ, and sorted by orderNumber the later-created order (lineCount 2) comes after the earlier one (lineCount 1). Create steps carry no status expectation because POST /api/widget_orders answers the known 500 although the row is saved.

OrdersIPlaced (where placedBy == $user.id) lists the caller's own order but not an order placed by someone else: the fixture row with placedBy 'qil-someone-else' exists (checked through the page endpoint) yet never appears in the query result, while the caller's own row (placedBy defaulted to the actor 'developer') does. Create steps carry no status expectation (known POST /api/widget_orders 500 with the row saved).

REG-301: AuditedCatalogEntries declares permissionRequirements [report.catalog.audit], which the generated manifest grants to the super-user only. A plain USER (${key_alice}) who reads the same concept through ActiveCatalogEntries (200) is refused AuditedCatalogEntries with 403 -- the refusal comes from the requirement, not from concept access -- while the super-user runs it (200).
